prompt: Most people earn modest incomes, but a long tail earns far more, pulling the average above the median.
tells: a long tail earns far more
why: A few very high incomes stretch the distribution to the right and pull the mean above the median. A long tail on one side is skew.
trap: One extreme value is an outlier; a long tail of them is skew.

prompt: Most posts get a few likes, while a small share get thousands, stretching the chart to the right.
tells: stretching the chart to the right
why: Most posts get a few likes and a handful get thousands, giving a long tail to the right. That's right-skewed data.
trap: It's a whole tail, not one point.

prompt: The exam was easy: most scored near 95, with a tail of low scores trailing left.
tells: a tail of low scores trailing left
why: Most scores bunch near 95 with a few low scores trailing to the left. A long tail toward low values is left skew.
trap: Several low scores form a tail.

prompt: The histogram of wait times is lopsided, piled up near zero with a long right tail.
why: Wait times pile up near zero and a few stretch much longer, so the shape is lopsided with a long right tail. That's skewed data.

prompt: Because the data is so lopsided, the mean sits far from where most values are.
tells: the mean sits far from where most values are
why: The few extreme values in the tail pull the mean away from where most values sit. A mean far from the bulk is a sign of skew.
trap: It's the shape, not the mean itself, that's being described.

prompt: Most app sessions are short, and the tail of long sessions keeps going.
tells: the tail of long sessions keeps going
why: Most sessions are short but a long tail of very long ones keeps going to the right. That's right-skewed data.
